issue_context.title: Extend System.Runtime.Intrinsics.X86 to support nint and nuint
comments: If the intrinsics are already built in on the C++ side and only the C# implementation is missing, I'd be happy to take a look when I have time. @tannergooding Feel free to assign me (unless it's something extremely urgent).

review_comments:
@tannergooding 
Hi Tanner, do you know why this is also failing (PlatformNotSupportedException)?

**intrinsic definition:**
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/369fdcd5bc0da85fda4b12ae35e03128c2006f10/src/coreclr/jit/hwintrinsiclistxarch.h#L389
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/369fdcd5bc0da85fda4b12ae35e03128c2006f10/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Runtime/Intrinsics/X86/Sse2.cs#L700

**codegen:**
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/369fdcd5bc0da85fda4b12ae35e03128c2006f10/src/coreclr/jit/hwintrinsiccodegenxarch.cpp#L1290

**lowering:**
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/369fdcd5bc0da85fda4b12ae35e03128c2006f10/src/coreclr/jit/lowerxarch.cpp#L6041

This file seems like a lot of code for testing these scenarios.

I'd expect we already have some of this functionality supported -or- that simply testing the "basic" scenario would be sufficient here.

There's changes here where I'd expect none. It looks like `float`/`double` got moved up and its messing up the diffs.

This would likely explain your build failures as well
I would, in general, expect this whole file to be "purely additive" (no lines modified/removed) with just the new `nint`/`nuint` APIs being additions

The format we use for Arm/Arm64 is:
```
__m128i _mm256_extractf128_si256 (__m256i a, const int imm8)
  x86: VEXTRACTF128 xmm/m128, ymm, imm8
  x64: VEXTRACTF128 xmm/m128, ymm, imm8
```

In this case its identical for both so we can just use the normal form instead:
```
__m128i _mm256_extractf128_si256 (__m256i a, const int imm8)
  VEXTRACTF128 xmm/m128, ymm, imm8
```
